notes: §1985:VI.5.3.2 prints three formats: Format 1, a level-number, an optional data-name-1 or FILLER, and at most one each of REDEFINES, PICTURE, USAGE, SIGN, OCCURS (fixed or DEPENDING ON), SYNCHRONIZED, JUSTIFIED, BLANK WHEN ZERO and VALUE IS literal-1; Format 2, 66 data-name-1 RENAMES; Format 3, 88 condition-name-1 with VALUE IS or VALUES ARE. The grammar rule dataDescriptionEntry parses a level-number, an optional name and either the clause list or the RENAMES body; ClosedFormatPass.ScreenClauseRepetition refuses any clause written twice from the ClauseCardinalities row (COBOL2423), whose order is free as §1985:VI.5.3.3 SR2 frees it ("The remaining clauses may be written in any order."), and VisitUnrecognizedDataClause refuses anything the format does not print (COBOL1941). LevelNumberPass.VisitLevelNumber and CheckEntryFormat hold the level to 01 through 49, 66, 77 and 88 and each special level to its format (EntryNameObligation: a name is required on 66, 77 and 88, the 77 half being §1985:VI.5.2.1's list of required clauses, "2. data-name"); DataBinder.BindEntry and BindCondition bind Formats 1 and 3, and NarrowToDataDivisionFormats holds OCCURS to the two printed forms. 1985 needs no arm for what it shares with 2023; what 2023 adds is refused at 85 by the VersionConformancePass gates (VisitTypedefClause and its siblings for TYPE, SAME AS, ALIGNED, ANY LENGTH, BASED, DYNAMIC LENGTH, GROUP-USAGE and PROPERTY, VisitConstantEntryBody, VisitValidationClause, VisitOccursClause for OCCURS DYNAMIC, VisitPictureClause for the LOCALE phrase), while EXTERNAL and GLOBAL stay, being the Inter-Program module's (§1985:X.4.3.2). The witness declares FILLER, REDEFINES, USAGE, OCCURS, SIGN, JUSTIFIED, BLANK WHEN ZERO, a level 88 and a level 66 and shows each working. Probed further at --std 85 (66 entries): every clause in its long and short spelling, an entry with no name at 01 and 05, one-digit levels and level 49 are accepted; no level-number, no period, levels 00, 50, 78 and 001, each clause twice, two names, REDEFINES after PICTURE, a 66 that is FILLER, unnamed, without RENAMES or with PICTURE, an 88 that is FILLER or unnamed, 77 FILLER, OCCURS DEPENDING without TO, INDEXED BY before the KEY phrase, OCCURS 0, SYNC LEFT RIGHT, JUSTIFIED LEFT, SEPARATE without LEADING or TRAILING, BLANK WHEN ZEROS and each later-edition clause are refused.

next.reason: Amendment 1 (X3.23a-1989, its change for page VI-20 (T): 'delete the box around the first occurrence' of [INDEXED BY {index-name-1} ...]) moved a level-2 box only, a typographical error; the syntax is what it was and the box is no difference. §1985:VI.5.3.2 Format 1 is level-number [data-name-1 | FILLER] [REDEFINES] [PICTURE] [USAGE BINARY | COMPUTATIONAL | COMP | DISPLAY | INDEX | PACKED-DECIMAL] [SIGN] [OCCURS, fixed or DEPENDING ON] [SYNCHRONIZED] [JUSTIFIED] [BLANK WHEN ZERO] [VALUE 'IS literal-1']; Format 2 is 66 RENAMES; Format 3 is 88 VALUE(S). §2023:13.16.2 carries all three (Format 3 as '88 condition-name-1 value-clause'), spelling REDEFINES, BLANK WHEN ZERO, JUSTIFIED, SIGN and SYNCHRONIZED in place and naming 'entry-name-clause' and the occurs, picture, usage and value clauses, whose formats are §2023:13.18.20.2, §2023:13.18.38.2, §2023:13.18.40.2, §2023:13.18.60.2 and §2023:13.18.63.2; the clause formats §2023:13.18.8.2 (BLANK WHEN ZERO), §2023:13.18.32.2 (JUSTIFIED), §2023:13.18.33.2 ('level-number'), §2023:13.18.44.2 (REDEFINES), §2023:13.18.45.2 ('66 data-name-1' RENAMES), §2023:13.18.52.2 (SIGN) and §2023:13.18.55.2 (SYNCHRONIZED) restate the parts the entry format spells in place. Every 1985 entry keeps its meaning, but 2023 accepts entries the 1985 format refuses: TYPEDEF, ALIGNED, ANY LENGTH, BASED, CONSTANT RECORD, DYNAMIC LENGTH, GROUP-USAGE, PROPERTY, SAME AS, SELECT WHEN, TYPE 'type-name-1', 'validation-clauses' and 'Format 4 (validation)', and through the named clauses the new usages, the dynamic-capacity OCCURS and the table VALUE. EXTERNAL and GLOBAL are not among the additions: the 1985 inter-program format has them (§1985:X.4.3.2). Compile-time only.
